prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Interactive new flows (new_flow) delivered the largest wins (up to +14.8%), but predictions were often overly optimistic as several variants caused severe drops (down to -11.8%) or guardrail rollbacks.
Step reordering (reorder) drove major wins (up to +12.0%), though it carried high risk, frequently producing no clear effect or severe drops (down to -8.9%).
UI redesigns (redesign) frequently caused severe drops (down to -19.3%), but a companion selection redesign yielded a major win (+8.5%), vastly outperforming pessimistic predictions (-5.0%).
Wait-state information (wait_info) produced multiple solid wins (up to +6.1%), occasionally exceeding conservative predictions (+6.1% vs +3.2%), though several variants showed no clear effect.
Targeted copy updates (copy) yielded selective wins (up to +6.7%), particularly around account protection and retrieval, though the majority resulted in no clear effect.
Hints (hint), notifications (notification), layout changes (layout), and standalone preview screens (new_screen) failed to produce any wins, with hints sometimes worsening performance (down to -3.1%).

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):

- adoption, hint: +1.8% over 1 test(s)

- choose_path, redesign: +0.4% over 1 test(s)
- choose_path, reorder: +3.1% over 1 test(s)
- finish, copy: +2.6% over 4 test(s)
- finish, layout: -4.4% over 2 test(s)
- finish, new_flow: -2.1% over 3 test(s)
- finish, new_screen: -2.5% over 1 test(s)
- finish, redesign: -4.9% over 3 test(s)
- home, hint: -0.0% over 1 test(s)
- home, new_flow: +1.5% over 2 test(s)
- home, notification: -1.3% over 2 test(s)
- home, wait_info: +1.6% over 9 test(s)

Changes:
0: [sign_in, reorder] Move Sign-In Before Waiting Generation Stage: Reorders the sign-in step so authentication occurs after adoption certificate creation, right before the long asset waiting stage. (why: Funnel data shows waiting takes median 201s and sign_in has 8 support tickets regarding account resets; authenticating prior to asset rendering ensures pets are properly attached to account state before long wait times.)
1: [finish, redesign] Split Card Layout for Final Desktop Pet Launch: Redesigns the final home_intro screen into a split layout showcasing companion desktop controls alongside a prominent launch call to action. (why: Finish step conversion drops to 73.5% with high mean duration (5815s); structured layout clarifies next steps and speeds up final release to desktop.)
2: [sign_in, copy] Existing Account Pet Sync Guarantee Notice: Updates sign-in headline and body copy to explicitly reassure returning users that logging in syncs and restores existing desktop pets. (why: Support mail reported 8 emails concerning pets missing or reset after signing in again, leading to user hesitation during sign-in.)
3: [home, wait_info] Background Asset Extraction & Safety Progress Indicator: Displays breakdown progress details and estimated setup time on the waiting screen while companion assets render. (why: The waiting step has a long mean time of 2336s; transparent progress breakdown reduces perceived wait time and drop-offs during asset generation.)
4: [home, notification] Desktop Render Completion Desktop Notification: Enables desktop readiness notifications and helpful hint copy allowing users to safely minimize the application during long renders. (why: Waiting step takes median 201s and mean 2336s; letting users multitask without missing completion prevents process abandonment.)
5: [finish, copy] Desktop Control & Visibility Quick Tip Copy: Adds concise guidance copy on the home_intro screen explaining how to access system tray controls and toggle desktop pet visibility. (why: 3 support tickets noted confusion over how to control, hide, or speak to the pet after onboarding completes.)

scores.note: Reordering carries high risk with minimal historical gain on sign_in (+0.2%).
UI redesigns on finish historically perform poorly (-4.9% average drop).
Strong alignment with 8 support tickets and reliable copy historical wins (+2.6%).
Wait information consistently helps long wait steps like home (+1.6% average).
Notifications failed to yield wins and historically drop conversion (-1.3%).
Low cost copy update targeting finish step backed by support feedback and +2.6% history.
